name: Cloud Office
_doc: SOURCE BUILD, as of this commit. This directory used to be a MIRROR: ship-cloud-sheets.yml downloaded Collabora's official APK, checked it against a pinned sha256 and republished those exact bytes. That gave a strong supply-chain guarantee and zero ownership — we could not rename the app, could not move its menus, and above all could not make Text Enhance work, because the feature needs code inside the web layer and the Android shell. The owner chose ownership. So we now build from source, and the sha256-of-upstream's-bytes guarantee is replaced by a pinned-revision guarantee; see supply_chain below, which states plainly what is weaker.
_doc_no_source_in_git: THE SOURCE IS NOT IN THIS REPOSITORY AND MUST NOT BE. LibreOffice core with external/ present is multi-gigabyte; this repo has a hard rule that no file may approach 100 MB, has already had to repair a 90 MB repository, and shards its transcripts to stay under GitHub's blob limit. Committing the tree would wreck it. Instead: two pinned upstreams fetched at build time, and every edit we own as a numbered patch in patches/. The fleet's other forks (dialer, matrix, vault, media-center) vendor their patched source instead — they moved to that on 2026-08-19 — and we deliberately cannot follow them, for size and nothing else. patches/README.md justifies the divergence in full.

online._doc: Collabora Online — the web app in the WebView (browser/) AND the Android shell around it (android/). This is the ONLY tree we patch.
online._doc_url: GERRIT, NOT GITHUB, AND THAT IS NOT A PREFERENCE. The GitHub mirror (CollaboraOnline/online) carries the Android tree only on distro/collabora/co-25.04-mobile; the 26.04 mobile line — the one matching the 26.04.3.1 APK this app shipped while it was a mirror — exists only on Collabora's own Gerrit. Pinning the GitHub mirror would have quietly moved the owner back a whole release line. github_mirror stays recorded as a read-only convenience for code search; it is never the fetch source.
online._doc_revision: A COMMIT SHA, NOT A BRANCH. VERIFIED: patches/0001 applies cleanly to this exact revision with `git am --keep-non-patch` from a clean checkout, watched, not assumed. The SAME patch generated against 25.04-mobile FAILED here on three files — 'error: browser/src/map/Clipboard.js: patch does not apply' — which is precisely the silent drift a floating ref would have caused and the reason the sha is written down. tests/patches-apply.sh refuses anything that is not a full 40-character sha.
online._doc_patch_mode: apply = the series in patches/ is applied with `git am` at materialize time against `revision`. The fleet's other forks are `vendored` (patched source committed, patches kept only as history). Reading this field is how an engine tells the two apart without knowing which app it is looking at.

configure._doc: THE REBRAND IS THESE FLAGS, NOT A PATCH. android/app/appSettings.gradle is generated from android/app/appSettings.gradle.in, whose @APP_NAME@ / @APP_PACKAGE_NAME@ / @VENDOR@ / @INFO_URL@ placeholders configure.ac substitutes (AC_CONFIG_FILES, configure.ac:2923), so upstream already exposes every branding value as a knob. Patching the generated file would hardcode into the tree what a flag sets, and the patch would then conflict on every upstream touch of that file.
configure._doc_flag_names: EVERY NAME HERE IS VERIFIED AGAINST configure.ac AT THE PIN, BECAUSE AUTOCONF DOES NOT CHECK THEM FOR US. This block said "--with-android-package-name" from 05b0c6c15 until 2026-09-11. No such option exists at this revision — upstream's is --with-app-package-name (AC_ARG_WITH at configure.ac:292), and there is no @ANDROID_PACKAGE_NAME@ placeholder anywhere; the applicationId comes from @APP_PACKAGE_NAME@. An unknown --with-* does NOT fail configure: autoconf prints 'unrecognized options' to stderr and continues, so $with_app_package_name would have stayed empty and APP_PACKAGE_NAME would have taken its default. VERIFIED BY READING configure.ac:1155-1169: the default is org.collabora.app for an Android build, and com.collabora.office.Mobile only when enable_iosapp=yes. So the megabuild would have spent its money producing an APK whose applicationId is UPSTREAM'S, while android.application_id, the fleet manifest, the GHCR image and the launcher's installed-app probe all name com.diegonmarcos.cloudoffice — an app that would not exist. tests/test-configure-flags-exist.sh now derives the required flag from upstream on every run (placeholder -> configure.ac variable -> flag) and fails closed, so this cannot regress silently and a future upstream rename reports its new name instead of passing.

online._doc_fetch_cost: MEASURED, so nobody plans CI around a guess: Gerrit refuses blob filtering (`warning: filtering not recognized by server, ignoring`) and will not serve an arbitrary sha (`upload-pack: not our ref`). A `git fetch --depth 1 origin distro/collabora/co-26.04-mobile` from this container produced a 471 MB .git and took roughly ten minutes. Any CI step fetching this needs that budget and a cache; it is not a thirty-second checkout.

engine._doc: THE ENGINE IS A PINNED PREBUILT BINARY, NOT A BUILD. This key replaced upstream.core on 2026-09-11. WHAT CHANGED AND WHY: upstream.core pinned the separate LibreOffice `core` repo at c1013fad, read from a ref tip on 2026-09-10 and dated 2026-04-01 — five months stale against the 2026-09-03 shell it was supposed to match — and it existed so that #240 could pay for an NDK megabuild of LibreOffice. Nothing the owner asked for needs that build. patches/0001 touches nine files: five TypeScript/JavaScript in browser/, three Java/XML/JSON in android/, and settings.gradle. Not one line of C++. So both native libraries can be taken from the artefact we already pin and already trust, and the engine's own git ancestry stops being a build input at all — which is why there is no `revision` of a core repository here to keep in sync, and why Gerrit's refusal to serve arbitrary shas no longer matters to this app.
engine._doc_two_native_halves: READ FROM THE ARTEFACT, NOT ASSUMED. The APK carries FIFTEEN .so files, and #241's "one monolithic 199 MB library" is only the first of them. lib/arm64-v8a/liblo-native-code.so (199,472,488 bytes) is LAYER 1, the LibreOffice engine, the thing a megabuild would produce. lib/arm64-v8a/libandroidapp.so (6,322,632 bytes) is online's OWN C++ — wsd/, kit/, net/, common/ — and is the ONLY thing that needs the eight static archives and four header trees an APK cannot carry. The other thirteen are NSS and libc++. Because we change no C++, neither is rebuilt, and the link-time half stops being required.

source._doc: The bytes are the ones this app mirrored until 05b0c6c15, and they are the same bytes Collabora's F-Droid index publishes — verified 2026-09-10 by streaming all 267,216,449 through sha256sum, and re-downloaded and re-inspected in full on 2026-09-11. The sha256 is the whole security argument: extracting a pinned artefact at build time is exactly the guarantee the mirror already relied on, so the engine half of this app KEEPS the supply-chain property that supply_chain._doc_weaker says the source build gives up. Only the layers we actually edit lose it.
source._doc_not_committed: 199 MB CANNOT BE COMMITTED — twice GitHub's 100 MB blob cap, and this repository has already had to repair a 90 MB history. The workflow downloads this URL, checks the sha256, and unzips only the paths named below. Nothing binary enters git.

native_libs._doc: Lifted verbatim out of the pinned APK and dropped into online's OWN jniLibs source directory, which is where upstream's build puts them too: android/lib/build.gradle sets jniLibs.srcDirs = ['src/main/cpp/lib'], and CMakeLists.txt.in fills that directory with `cmake -E copy`, never with a compiler. A .so in a jniLibs source dir is PACKAGED, not built. Asserted on every run by tests/test-no-engine-build-required.sh against upstream at upstream.online.revision.
native_libs._doc_expect_count: All fifteen, by directory rather than by name: a hand-written list of .so files is a second copy of upstream's DT_NEEDED graph and goes stale the first time Collabora adds one. The count is the assertion — if the APK stops carrying exactly fifteen, the build stops rather than shipping an app that dlopens something that is not there.
native_libs._doc_verified_by_extraction: RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-11 BY EXTRACTING, not by reading the table. The ZIP central directory (6,375 entries, 591,403 bytes) was range-fetched and parsed: lib/arm64-v8a holds exactly 15 .so, expect_count agrees; 0 entries end .a, .h or .hxx, so the link-time half is confirmed absent; assets/dist holds 3,384 entries, which is the COOL web UI we rebuild. lib/arm64-v8a/libandroidapp.so and liblo-native-code.so are both STORED (compression method 0), so they can be lifted with a byte range and no inflate. libandroidapp.so was pulled out in full — 6,322,632 bytes, matching this table — and parsed as a 64-bit AArch64 ELF (e_machine 183). THE ENGINE CAN BE EXTRACTED; that question is closed and needs no further re-litigation.

assets._doc: The engine's DATA half — .rdb type libraries, fonts, share/registry, config — is likewise already built, and already in the APK. Upstream's copyUnpackAssets / copyAssets / createFullConfig gradle tasks read it out of ${liboInstdir}, i.e. out of an engine build tree; taking it from the artefact is the same files by a shorter road. assets/dist is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: that is layer 2, the COOL web UI, and it is the thing we rebuild.

engine_revision._doc: PROVENANCE, NOT A BUILD INPUT — and read out of the artefact rather than out of a ref tip. assets/program/versionrc in the pinned APK says buildid=20a46c332c38; that is the twelve-character form configure.ac:927 derives for CORE_VERSION_HASH, which means the prebuilt mode can read the hash from a file the APK actually contains instead of from instdir/program/setuprc, which it does not (tests/engine-artefacts.json records setuprc as in_apk=false). Nothing fetches this revision and nothing needs it to be an ancestor of anything.

engine._doc_license: SHIPPED UNMODIFIED AND DYNAMICALLY LINKED, WHICH IS THE EASY CASE. LibreOffice core is MPL-2.0; MPL is FILE-level copyleft, so an unmodified file carries no obligation beyond keeping the notice, and the APK already carries assets/license.html and assets/notice.txt (both checked as present by tests/engine-artefacts.json). We modify no engine file, so there is no modified engine source to publish; the files we DO modify are online's, are also MPL-2.0, and are already public as patches/0001 in a public repository. THE REAL CONSTRAINT IS NOT COPYLEFT, IT IS TRADEMARK: assets/dist/images carries collabora-office-white.svg, full-logo.svg and toolbar-bg-logo*.svg, and republishing those inside an app called Cloud Office is a Collabora trade-mark use, not a licence question. Upstream's own answer is the branding knobs we already set — --with-app-name, --with-vendor and APP_BRANDING_DIR — plus dropping those image assets. See a0_docs/eng-specs/cloud-office-prebuilt-engine-reuse.md; the fleet's licence-boundary guard models source copyleft only and has no way to express this yet.
engine._doc_BLOCKER_configure_gate: THE MECHANICAL THINGS STILL IN THE WAY. NONE IS A COMPILE, AND THERE ARE THREE, NOT ONE. This key said 'THE ONE MECHANICAL THING' until 2026-09-11 and named only the first; the other two were found by reading android/lib/build.gradle and android/lib/libSettings.gradle.in at the pin, and BOTH of them fail GREEN, which is worse than the one that fails loudly. (1) CONFIGURE GATE, and it is real: configure.ac:884 refuses --enable-androidapp without --with-lo-builddir, then probes that directory for instdir/program/setuprc (921), workdir/LinkTarget/StaticLibrary/liblibpng.a (930), Poco/Poco.h (1009-1012) and zstd.h/libzstd.a (1051-1058). tests/engine-artefacts.json records 0 of 6,375 APK entries ending .a/.h/.hxx, re-counted 2026-09-11, so the gate cannot be satisfied from the artefact. (2) GRADLE STILL RUNS THE NDK, AND TAKING libandroidapp.so PREBUILT DOES NOT STOP IT. android/lib/build.gradle declares externalNativeBuild in BOTH defaultConfig (lines 32-36) and the android block (74-79), pointing at src/main/cpp/CMakeLists.txt, whose add_library(androidapp SHARED ...) compiles online's own wsd/kit/net/common and links the eight static archives. So Gradle asks for the link-time half on every :lib build no matter what is already sitting in jniLibs, and #240 comes back by the side door. patches/0002 must remove that wiring, not just add a configure option. (3) THE ASSET TASKS READ AN ENGINE BUILD TREE AND FAIL SILENTLY. libSettings.gradle.in sets liboSrcRoot='@LOBUILDDIR@' and liboInstdir='@LOBUILDDIR@/instdir'; copyUnpackAssets, copyAssets and createFullConfig copy from ${liboInstdir}/program, /share and /share/fonts/truetype, and preBuild depends on them. A Gradle Copy task whose `from` does not exist SUCCEEDS AND COPIES NOTHING. In prebuilt mode that ships an APK with the engine's .so files present and its data half — .rdb type libraries, registry, fonts, config — ABSENT, after a fully green build. patches/0002 must disable these tasks explicitly in prebuilt mode so the behaviour is declared; relying on a missing directory to no-op is the same class of defect as the four testers that passed because ripgrep was absent. NOT WRITTEN YET. build.host therefore stays null — see build._doc_host.
engine._doc_jni_abi_is_verified: THE RISK #277 DID NOT WEIGH, NOW MEASURED AND CURRENTLY SAFE. Taking the native half prebuilt means OUR Java, compiled from upstream.online.revision, binds at runtime to COLLABORA'S libandroidapp.so, built for the 26.04.3.1-155 release. Those are different commits: the pin's own commit subject is 'fix(iOS): correct blank slides when presenting' (authored 2026-09-03, committed 2026-09-04 by Gerrit change 11099), an ordinary branch-tip commit and not that release tag. JNI binds BY SYMBOL NAME at first call, never at build time, so a native method added, removed or renamed between the two produces a signed, published, installable APK that dies with UnsatisfiedLinkError when the document view opens. MEASURED 2026-09-11 by extracting the .so from the pinned APK over byte ranges and reading its .dynsym: it exports exactly 8 Java_* symbols, all in org.libreoffice.androidlib (LOActivity 7, COWebViewClient 1), none of them a long overload name; the Java at the pin declares exactly those 8 and no others. They agree today. org.libreoffice.androidlib is the LIBRARY module's package and the rebrand does not touch it — --with-app-package-name sets applicationId only — so renaming the app to com.diegonmarcos.cloudoffice cannot break these symbols. tests/test-jni-abi-matches-prebuilt.sh re-checks the whole chain on every run and fails closed, so the day the pin moves away from the published bytes it reds instead of shipping a dead app.

supply_chain._doc: WHAT REPLACES THE sha256 PIN, AND WHAT IS GENUINELY WEAKER. Stated here rather than in a README because the next person to touch this will read build.json.
supply_chain._doc_before: BEFORE: one sha256 over Collabora's release APK. Strong and simple — the bytes either matched what Collabora published or the job failed. It also meant the app was signed by Collabora, and installing ours was byte-identical to installing from their F-Droid repo.
supply_chain._doc_after: AFTER: ONE pinned git revision (online, full sha, verified at fetch time by tests/patches-apply.sh) plus ONE pinned binary artefact (upstream.engine, sha256 over Collabora's own release APK), plus a patch series that must apply exactly or the build stops. This is a change from the 2026-09-10 shape, which pinned TWO git revisions because it expected to compile the engine. It does not any more: the engine ships prebuilt, so for the 199 MB that is most of this app the ORIGINAL sha256-of-Collabora's-bytes guarantee is still in force. A commit sha is a hash over a whole tree's history, so neither pin is a weaker hash — they hash different things.
supply_chain._doc_weaker: GENUINELY WEAKER, AND NARROWER THAN IT WAS. (1) We no longer verify a Collabora-SIGNED artefact; we verify its bytes by sha256 and then re-sign the repackaged result with the fleet key, so a compromise of that key now reaches Cloud Office where before it could not. (2) The layers we rebuild — the COOL web bundle and the Android shell — are built by us from pinned source, so for those the guarantee is source-and-toolchain rather than published-bytes. WHAT IS NO LONGER WEAK, and was on 2026-09-10: the engine. Taking it as a sha256-pinned prebuilt means no NDK toolchain, no external/ tarball tree and no engine build host enter the trust surface at all. The honest summary: we trade a narrow verifiable guarantee for ownership, over the ~20 percent of the APK we actually change.
supply_chain._doc_reproducible: Reproducible in the sense that matters here: same two pins + same patch series + same configure flags + same toolchain = same source going into the compiler. Bit-identical APK output is NOT claimed and should not be until someone has actually diffed two builds.

android._doc_application_id: OURS NOW, AND IT CANNOT BE UPSTREAM'S. com.collabora.libreoffice belongs to bytes signed with Collabora's key; a rebuilt app signed with the fleet key cannot claim it, and Android would refuse the install anyway (signature mismatch on update). WHAT THE OWNER WILL EXPERIENCE: the new app does NOT replace the installed Collabora Office. It installs alongside it, as a second launcher icon, and the two coexist — different package names are different apps to Android in every respect. Documents opened by file association will offer both until the old one is removed. Nothing migrates automatically: the old app's settings and recent-files list stay with the old app. Removing the old one is a manual uninstall and is safe, because Collabora Office stores documents in normal storage rather than in its private data directory.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps. Cloud Office MUST be inside that set and this is not optional here: Text Enhance crosses an application boundary to the Cloud Keyboard over ITextTools, which is guarded by com.diegonmarcos.cloud.permission.CONSTELLATION_DATA at protectionLevel=signature. Signed with anything else, the platform refuses the bind and Text Enhance cannot work at all — it would fail with 'Text tools need the Cloud Keyboard app' on a phone where the keyboard is plainly installed. build.sh::_resolve_signing resolves the key from $VAULT_DIR + sops and FAILS LOUD if it cannot; there is no fallback and no generated key. See SIGNING.md.

build._doc: WE DO NOT BUILD THIS ANYWHERE IN THIS REPO'S NORMAL CI. An NDK megabuild over LibreOffice core plus the whole external/ tree does not fit a standard GitHub-hosted runner in either time or disk. The host is a CONFIGURATION VALUE, deliberately, so that choosing it is a separate decision from this work — a sibling task is establishing which host can carry the compile, and nothing here bakes in an answer.
build._doc_host: null = no build host has been established yet, and the workflow must FAIL LOUDLY rather than fall back to a hosted runner that will die four hours in with a full disk. DELIBERATELY STILL NULL ON 2026-09-11, AND SETTING IT WAS THE ASKED-FOR CHANGE. It was left null because a non-null host is not a build, and this app's entire history is green runs that published nothing — setting the field while nothing can build would have moved the lie from the workflow into this file. Three things must exist first, and none did: patches/0002 (all three blockers in upstream.engine._doc_BLOCKER_configure_gate, not just the configure one); an ac_cloud-sheets/build.sh plus a cloud-sheets fork engine, which this directory does NOT have — it holds only build.json, README.md, patches/ and tests/, while every other fork app ships build.sh with materialize-fork/build-fork; and a source-build workflow to replace the mirror. NOTE ALSO THAT 'ubuntu-latest is expected to be enough' IS UNTESTED: android/{app,lib}/build.gradle at the pin ask for compileSdk 37, buildToolsVersion 37.0.0 and ndkVersion 29.0.14206865, and whether a hosted runner can install those has never been checked. Nothing else in this file changes when the host is finally set.

text-tools._doc: Shared BY REFERENCE from ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/text-tools — the ITextTools binder contract and its client, the same directory cloud-mail and the Cloud Keyboard build. materialize places it at android/text-tools inside the fetched online tree; patch 0001's settings.gradle include expects it there. A COPY MUST NEVER BE VENDORED: the AIDL's method order is a wire format, and two copies that disagree about it make an installed keyboard answer the wrong call.

text_enhance._doc: Cloud Office is a CALLER of the fleet enhancer, never a second copy of it. Routing, the model registry, the prompt chunking for oversized input, the timeout and the provider API KEY all stay in the Cloud Keyboard behind ITextTools; this app calls enhanceWith(), which exists precisely so a caller can hold its own settings and hand over its whole decision. cloud-mail was split from the keyboard the same way and for the same reason.
text_enhance._doc_settings_are_not_shared: The owner's standing rule: a user-editable settings surface is an independently editable copy per app, never a shared link. What is shared is the network transport and the credential. Cloud Office's own choices live in its own SharedPreferences file ('cloud_text_enhance') with defaults from android/lib/src/main/assets/cloud_text_enhance.json, added by patch 0001.

tests._doc: WITHOUT THIS BLOCK NONE OF THIS APP'S TESTERS HAD EVER RUN, and nothing said so. cloud-android-test-engine.sh resolves .tests.shell.dir and DEFAULTS TO "test"; this app's directory is "tests", so the engine looked at ac_cloud-sheets/test, found nothing, printed one COVERAGE-GAP line and exited 0. The second half of the same defect is the glob: the engine runs only "$dir"/test-*.sh, and both testers here were named without that prefix, so even with the directory right they would have been skipped. Two files that call themselves 'the assertion the whole clone structure rests on' and the evidence behind the #241 verdict were decoration. Fixed by declaring the directory and by renaming the artefact tester to test-engine-artefacts-in-apk.sh.

shell._doc_requires: Checked BEFORE any tester runs, because a tester that shells out to a missing tool does not fail — it answers from the tool's absence. test-engine-artefacts-in-apk.sh parses a ZIP central directory in python3 and range-fetches it with curl; test-configure-flags-exist.sh reads Gerrit's REST API with curl and decodes base64. Absent any of these, both would report a verdict they never computed.
shell._doc_not_a_tester: patches-apply.sh IS DELIBERATELY NOT NAMED test-*.sh, and that is a decision rather than the accident above. It is the strongest assertion this app has — it fetches the pin and applies the series for real — but Gerrit refuses both blob filtering and sha fetches, so it measured 471 MB and about ten minutes from this container. That is the wrong shape for a per-push tester on a workflow that triggers on every commit under ac_cloud-sheets/**, and a ten-minute network step on every doc edit is how a suite starts getting ignored. It belongs to the source-build workflow as a release gate, run once against the pin, and to agents by hand. When build.host is set and that workflow exists, it gets an explicit step there — not this prefix.

variants._doc: arm64-v8a only, as the mirror was. Every additional ABI is another full NDK megabuild of LibreOffice core, and no phone in this fleet needs one.

auto_update._doc_require_unmetered_network: Still the largest artifact in the fleet by an order of magnitude. Unmetered-only so a background auto-update pass cannot burn a mobile data plan.

published_artifact._doc: WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE RELEASE SHELF RIGHT NOW, AND IT IS NOT OURS. Every other key in this file describes the app we intend to build. NOTHING HAS EVER BUILT IT: build.host is null and ship-cloud-sheets.yml exits 1 before it publishes anything. So the only office artefact on the rolling `latest` release is still Cloud-Sheets.apk from the mirror era, and it is Collabora's own signed build republished under our release name. This block records that as DATA rather than leaving it as prose in a commit message, because the repository had already started reasoning as though the source build existed — test-sheets-mirror-pin.sh deleted its published-bytes checks on the stated premise 'we build com.diegonmarcos.cloudoffice, we are its only source', which is false and stays false until #240 is funded.
published_artifact._doc_verified: READ OUT OF THE ARTEFACT ON 2026-09-10, not inferred from the filename. The ZIP central directory was range-fetched (6,375 entries), AndroidManifest.xml was decoded for its package attribute, META-INF/COLLABOR.RSA was decoded with openssl for the signing certificate, and all 267,216,449 bytes were streamed through sha256sum. All four agree with the row Collabora's own F-Droid index publishes for their arm64 APK, so these bytes are byte-identical to what their repo serves.
published_artifact.signer_subject: C=GB, L=Cambridge, O=Collabora Productivity Limited, OU=productivity, CN=Tomaz Vajngerl
published_artifact._doc_do_not_rename: DO NOT RENAME OR DELETE THIS ASSET AS A TIDY-UP. aa_cloud-superapp/build.json's phone-apps entry points install_apk_url at this exact filename, and it is the only office app the owner can install today. Renaming it hands him a 404; deleting it takes his office suite away to fix a labelling problem. The honest fix is to publish Cloud-Office.apk beside it, which needs a build host, not a rename.
published_artifact._doc_why_not_repackaged: AND IT MUST NOT BE REPACKAGED. Injecting our dex into these bytes to make the Text Enhance menu item appear would break Collabora's signature, require re-signing with the fleet key, and put a modified binary of unclear provenance on the owner's phone while looking like a successful build. #241 answered the reuse question NO on the engine's own terms: 0 of 6,375 entries are .a or .h, and upstream needs eight static archives to link libandroidapp.so.

_doc_source_identity: source_identity.mode="pin" IS DELIBERATELY GONE. It existed because a mirror's output was a pure function of `upstream`, so hashing the directory republished 250 MB whenever an unrelated repo-wide commit moved the tree sha — which happened on 2026-09-01. That reasoning DIES with the mirror: our output is now a function of the pins AND the patch series AND the configure flags, all of which live in this directory. Falling back to the default path hash is therefore correct, and leaving mode=pin would have been an active bug — every patch added here would have produced a byte-different APK that the gate believed was unchanged, and the phones would never have seen it.
